BillHeading.Sponsors: Representatives G. Hunt, Shea, Taylor, Young, Klippert, Dent, Haler, Wilcox, Short, Wilson, Scott, Condotta, Harris, Schmick, and Buys
BillHeading.BriefDescription: Referring a full repeal of Initiative Measure No. 594 to the people.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to criminal and public safety background checks for gun sales and transfers; repealing RCW 9.41.092, 9.41.113, 9.41.115, 9.41.137, and 82.08.833; repealing 2015 c ss 2, 5, 6, 7, and 11; repealing 2015 c 1 s 1 (uncodified); and providing for submission of this act to a vote of the people.

BillSectionHeader.P: The following acts or parts of acts are each repealed:

BillSection.P: 1RCW 9.41.092 (Licensed dealer deliveries—Background checks) and 2015 c 1 s 4 (Initiative Measure No. 594);
2RCW 9.41.113 (Firearm sales or transfers—Background checks—Requirements—Exceptions) and 2015 c 1 s 3 (Initiative Measure No. 594);
3RCW 9.41.115 (Penalties—Violations of RCW 9.41.113) and 2015 c 1 s 9 (Initiative Measure No. 594);
4RCW 9.41.137 (Department of licensing, authority to adopt rules—Reporting of violations—Authority to revoke licenses) and 2015 c 1 s 8 (Initiative Measure No. 594);
5RCW 82.08.833 (Exemptions—Sales or transfers of firearms—Unlicensed persons—Background check requirements) and 2015 c 1 s 10 (Initiative Measure No. 594);

BillSectionHeader.P: The secretary of state shall submit this act to the people for their adoption and ratification, or rejection, at the next general election to be held in this state, in accordance with Article II, section 1 of the state Constitution and the laws adopted to facilitate its operation.
